minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved several small wetland filings and set a 300-a-day fine deadline for 615 Townsend Street.
minutes.summary: The commission met by Zoom and worked through routine wetland filings: a field change, four negative determinations, two notices of intent, and continuances to August 17th. It also covered old business and enforcement, including trees cut by the DPW on Horizon Island causeway and a compliance deadline on the Townsend Street order.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted that the 615 Townsend Street enforcement order be fulfilled and verified by September 7th, or a daily fine applies.
It approved two notices of intent: a permeable paver patio at 172 Peninsula Drive and a retaining wall replacement at 207 Fire Road 16.
It issued negative determinations for 75 West Street (with fill removal and planting), 611 Goodrich Street and a dock at 755 Reservoir Road.
The 408 Electric Ave filing and four McSweeney notices of intent were continued to August 17th; 408 Electric Ave needs a more detailed plan.
On the Horizon Island causeway tree cutting, the agent will issue an administrative determination for ratification at the next meeting.

why_it_matters: Wetland filings and enforcement orders set what neighbors and landowners may build or must restore near wetlands, and a daily fine is a direct cost to a property owner who misses a deadline.
watch_next: August 17th meeting: continued filings for 408 Electric Ave and the McSweeney lots, and ratification of the Horizon Island determination.
September 7th: deadline for verified completion of the 615 Townsend Street enforcement order.
